title: The Food Safety Mitt
description: Six pictures from our own kitchens, one step each. This is not a memory test — every answer is in the picture above it. The point is that the mitt is a food safety tool, not a heat glove, and that one hand stays clean from the cooler all the way to the basket.

questions.title: Pepper has just pulled a Food Safety Mitt out of the box on top of the cooler. What is it actually for?
choices: Protecting her hand from the hot oil
Keeping her hand warm while she is in the cooler
Keeping bare skin off the bag, so nothing from her hand reaches the product
Marking her as the person running the fryer this shift
questions.help: Watch it through once before you answer. You can watch it again as many times as you like.
questions.explanation:
It is a food safety tool, not a heat glove.

• Thin plastic. It would do nothing against 350°F oil, and it never goes near it.
• Its whole job is to sit between your hand and the bag, so whatever is on your hands stays on your hands.

If you have thought of it as the fryer glove, that is the thing to unlearn. That belief is how people end up taking it to the fryer — the one place it must never go.

questions.title: The mitt is on. Which hand opens the cooler door?
choices: The bare hand, so the mitted hand stays clean for the bag
The mitted hand, since it is already covered
Either one, as long as she washes up afterwards
Neither — she should use a cloth on the handle
questions.help: One hand is doing a job. The other is being kept out of the way on purpose.
questions.explanation:
The bare hand opens the door. Look at the picture: the mitted hand is held clear, touching nothing.

• That handle is one of the dirtiest things in the kitchen — every hand in the building has been on it today.
• The moment the mitt touches it, the mitt is no cleaner than the handle, and raw product is the next thing it touches.

Opening a door with your awkward hand feels silly. It is the whole reason the mitt works.

And if the mitt does touch the handle: bin it, blue towel the handle and anything else that hand has been on, wash up, fresh mitt. You do not start the batch again.

questions.title: She is carrying the bag in the mitted hand. Before the bag is empty, what else may that mitted hand touch?
choices: The basket handle
The cooler door, to push it shut behind her
Her apron, to steady the bag
Nothing at all — only the bag
questions.help: Count the things the mitted hand is touching in the picture.
questions.explanation:
Only the bag. Plastic to plastic, cooler to basket, nothing in between.

The handle, the door, your apron, your phone — touch any of them and the mitt has picked something up. It stops being a barrier and becomes a carrier.

If you do touch something, that mitt is finished. Bin it and take a fresh one. They cost pennies.

questions.title: The wings are going into the basket. Where is the basket while that happens?
choices: Over the fryer, so nothing drops on the floor
On a sheet pan on the prep station
In the hand sink
On the shelf inside the cooler
questions.help: The basket is sitting on something in the picture. What is under it?
questions.explanation:
On a sheet pan on the prep station — never over the fryer.

• Breading, ice and crumbs fall off a frozen portion as it goes in.
• Over the oil, every one of them burns and darkens the whole vat — for every basket after yours, not just this one.

The sheet pan catches all of it and goes in the wash. That is the only reason it is there.

questions.title: The bag is empty. What happens to the bag and the mitt now?
choices: Keep the mitt on — there is still a basket to drop
Mitt in her pocket, ready for the next portion
Both go in the bin, right now, before she touches anything else
Rinse the mitt in the sanitizer bucket and use it again
questions.help: This picture is from a different store, so the room looks different. The bin is the thing to look at.
questions.explanation:
Both go in the bin, together, straight away.

• The bag and the mitt are one disposable item. The moment the bag is empty, the mitt has done its job.
• The sanitizer bucket is for cloths and surfaces. Rinsing a mitt and carrying on is worse than not wearing one, because you think you are protected.
• A mitt in a pocket comes out dirty.

This is the step that disappears when the store is busy. It is the one to be stubborn about.

questions.title: She is at the fryer with the basket and both of her hands are bare. Why is that right?
choices: The oil has not come up to temperature yet, so it cannot burn her
The mitt is food safety equipment, not heat protection — its job ended at the basket
She will put a fresh mitt on once the basket is in the oil
The basket handle is insulated, so no mitt is needed here
questions.help: Think back to the first question in this test.
questions.explanation:
Because the mitt was never protective equipment. It went in the bin two steps ago and nothing replaces it.

This is where the misunderstanding does real damage: someone who thinks the mitt is a fryer glove keeps it on for exactly this moment — and thin plastic near 350°F oil is a hazard, not a help.

Bare hands and a basket handle is what correct looks like at the fryer. If your hands are not bare by the time you get here, something went wrong earlier.

questions.title: Put the whole thing in order, start to finish.
steps: Wash and sanitize your hands at the dedicated hand sink
Put a Food Safety Mitt on one hand
Open the cooler with the bare hand and lift the bag out with the mitted one
Tip the product into a basket sitting on a sheet pan on the fry prep station
Bin the empty bag, shake the mitt off your hand and bin that too
Shake the basket over the sheet pan to knock off the loose crumbs
Lower the basket into an open lane of the fryer
questions.help: Two of these steps are not in any of the pictures. They still have their place in the order.
questions.explanation:
Hands, mitt, cooler, basket on the pan, bin the bag and mitt, shake off the crumbs, then the oil.

The two steps with no picture:
• The hand sink comes first. The mitt covers one hand, not both, and it does nothing about what is already on them.
• Shake the basket over the sheet pan before it goes in. Loose breading burns and darkens the vat for everybody after you.

Notice where the mitt stops — in the bin, before the basket is anywhere near the fryer. Everything after that is bare hands, which is why there is no such thing as taking the mitt to the oil.
